#
Dear Supporter,

West Virginia’s early voting begins on May 1. With two challengers for the Agriculture Commissioner’s office, this will be an especially important primary election for us. Many races will be decided on Tuesday, May 14th. Voter turnout will be particularly important for many good candidates.

The statistics are clear. My team and I have reduced regulations, increased Agriculture growth, and encouraged more young farmers than at any time in the past. All of this was accomplished with a budget much the same as 2008. We have demonstrated good prudent fiscal government decisions. We have consistently contributed to our state's record budget surpluses.

I believe my team in the Agriculture Department, and I are in a good position to win re-election. The fact that I am in a 3-way primary race may increase the chance that something could go wrong. I would rather not take that chance, so I continue crisscrossing the state, whenever I am not performing duties that you have twice elected me to do. It could make a significant difference!

My volunteers and I are preparing to face the unknown if it appears and we are getting ready for the General election in November. I am hoping you will agree with my strategy and contribute to my re-election.

We made it simple: go to [www.kentforwv.com](https://kentforwv.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=11e98a41f355b31f9f4041a29&id=ccad180f32&e=2e56df4f78) to pay or mail a check to the address below. Print and cut the form below with your information and mail with your check to. Thank you in advance for your support and vote.

body:
Support truth in local media with Broad + Liberty | | | |
---
| | | Dear Supporter:

We're not merely offering criticism – _Broad + Liberty_ is taking action to provide a solution.

Truth-seeking investigative reporting, a space to explore unconventional or disruptive ideas and viewpoints, open dialogue surrounding state and local issues – that is what _Broad + Liberty_ is building in our region.

As our local, state, and national media have increasingly drifted away from truth-seeking in favor of narratives and agendas, _Broad + Liberty_ is a locally-based nonprofit media outlet dedicated to the free exchange of ideas, giving voice to those who have been "shut out" by the legacy media, and providing oxygen to ideas that will improve the quality of life and governance in our region.

**Every day, we pursue a more perfect union with the help of our readers and donors**.

**_Broad + Liberty_ is growing, and with so much more work to be done.**

We are building a publication with cross-platform reach that is influencing policy outcomes, informing the leaders who serve us, and resonating in the hearts and minds of our readers, through news, editorials, and now multimedia content for those seeking straightforward perspectives grounded in reality.

**We couldn't do this without you – every dollar received is a spark that ignites change in our region and beyond.**

The work of _Broad + Liberty_ is essential in the movement for freedom – we are asking for your support to achieve our goals in the form of a [tax-deductible contribution](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=87a78538fe&e=b7b3eddce2) of any amount.

Thank you for your consideration,

The Editors at _Broad + Liberty_

subject: The Squad has shifted the trajectory of American politics
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

This is a long but important email about what we’ve accomplished together
with all of you and the Squad so far, and why we need your support to
protect our progressive power in Congress. [ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jdem-pts-email-jd-2.48vO86&refcode=em20240425-34484&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1001&akid=34484%2E1203867%2EVMrB6n ]I hope you’ll take a moment
to read it and pitch in whatever you can afford to help protect the Squad
in 2024 before Tuesday's deadline.

Over the last three cycles, alongside so many, our movement has been
instrumental in building real power in the U.S. House by electing some of
the most progressive, diverse, working-class representatives Congress has
seen in our lifetime — leaders like Cori Bush, Jamaal Bowman, Summer Lee,
Ilhan Omar, Rashida Tlaib, and the rest of the Squad.

Despite all the odds stacked against us, we’ve not only succeeded in
electing these true representatives of the people – we have fundamentally
reset what we expect from our elected officials: the urgency they bring to
office and how much they are willing to put their political capital and
power on the line to fight for the most vulnerable among us. The Squad has
fundamentally shifted the trajectory of American politics and has done it
all on our behalf.

Each of these progressive champions has led the fight for Medicare for
All, a Green New Deal, a livable minimum wage, racial justice, student
debt relief, and so much more. While we continue the work to make some of
these bold, necessary policies a reality, the Squad has brought a whole
lot of good to their communities and the country at large.

During their time in Congress, the Squad has delivered more than $4
billion to their districts to fund infrastructure, K-12 public education,
affordable housing, firefighting, climate resilience, public transit,
health centers, senior housing, employment assistance, and so much more.

They’ve stood with striking workers on picket lines, demanded an extension
of the federal evictions moratorium during the pandemic, and pushed for
the largest investment in clean energy and climate action ever through the
Inflation Reduction Act.

They were also among the very first to introduce a ceasefire resolution
and call for peace and the release of all Palestinian and Israeli hostages
back in October, despite cruel attacks from colleagues on both sides of
the aisle.

As a result, the Squad has angered Republicans, billionaires, and war
hawks alike; that’s why AIPAC and their right-wing megadonor network are
spending $100 million against them this cycle to try removing them from
office.

Corporate PACs have spent millions against us in the past and failed to
beat our people power. These attacks are proof that what we’re doing is
working — so we can’t let them set us back this year.

That’s why Justice Democrats and more than ten progressive partner

clean_body: [1]Justice Democrats Peter, This is a long but important email about what we’ve accomplished together with all of you and the Squad so far, and why we need your support to protect our progressive power in Congress. [ ]I hope you’ll take a moment to read it and pitch in whatever you can afford to help protect the Squad in 2024 before Tuesday's deadline. Over the last three cycles, alongside so many, our movement has been instrumental in building real power in the U.S. House by electing some of the most progressive, diverse, working-class representatives Congress has seen in our lifetime — leaders like Cori Bush, Jamaal Bowman, Summer Lee, Ilhan Omar, Rashida Tlaib, and the rest of the Squad. Despite all the odds stacked against us, we’ve not only succeeded in electing these true representatives of the people – we have fundamentally reset what we expect from our elected officials: the urgency they bring to office and how much they are willing to put their political capital and power on the line to fight for the most vulnerable among us. The Squad has fundamentally shifted the trajectory of American politics and has done it all on our behalf. Each of these progressive champions has led the fight for Medicare for All, a Green New Deal, a livable minimum wage, racial justice, student debt relief, and so much more. While we continue the work to make some of these bold, necessary policies a reality, the Squad has brought a whole lot of good to their communities and the country at large. During their time in Congress, the Squad has delivered more than $4 billion to their districts to fund infrastructure, K-12 public education, affordable housing, firefighting, climate resilience, public transit, health centers, senior housing, employment assistance, and so much more. They’ve stood with striking workers on picket lines, demanded an extension of the federal evictions moratorium during the pandemic, and pushed for the largest investment in clean energy and climate action ever through the Inflation Reduction Act. Folks,

I'm up a creek without a paddle, and my pirogue just sprung a huge leak.

I'm giving it all I got to stand up for you and our Conservative values, but everywhere I turn, there are more and more of them woke loonies.

There is so much at stake this election year, and so many good Democrats running who are worthy of your support. **I want to take a second to explain, in 3 points, why you should invest in this race to defeat Jim Jordan, if you would hear me out:****

[1]** No one has ever waged this strong of a challenge to Jim Jordan. He is in the fight of his life now, because we have built a formidable campaign together, {{FirstName_friend}}.**

[2]** The tide is turning against election deniers and extremists like Jordan who are opposed to reproductive rights and democracy. Voters in Ohio just reaffirmed these values, including support for abortion rights, and Jordan continues to stand in their way...let’s make sure he does so at his peril. **

[3]** Jim Jordan nearly became Speaker of the House last year, and he has made it no secret that he would try again should the opportunity arise. _Jordan was within a handful of votes of becoming second in the line of presidential succession_ —an outcome we cannot allow to happen.

Jim Jordan is weak, has done nothing for the people of my district, and he knows we can defeat him this year. **That is why I need your support. If you can make a contribution to this campaign of $25, $50, $100 or more today, you will help us defeat Trump’s favorite MAGA protege and restore civility and common sense to Congress again.

Friends,
In a recent radio interview, I was asked how I would improve constituent engagement and outreach in our district as its next Congressman. It's my favorite question. It would go something like this...
#1 — Show up.
#2 — Listen.
It's not exactly a novel idea, but it's sorely missed by our district because of a lack of representation. Our current representative, Republican Rep. Jack Bergman, doesn't even live here.

subject: My friend Sarah McBride
body:
Sarah McBride will be a changemaker in Congress. With your support, we will break barriers and deliver for the people.
#
**Sarah McBride will be a changemaker in Congress.**
Just look at what she’s already accomplished. Sarah passed paid family and medical leave, the largest expansion of Delaware's social safety net in decades. She’s a proven legislator.
And as the parent of a trans child, I am incredibly proud to support Sarah's campaign to be the first openly trans person elected to any federal office. This is a monumental moment for the LGBTQIA+ rights movement.
With your support, we will break barriers and deliver for the people.
In order to do that, we’ll need as much grassroots support as possible to protect her and our progressive movement from the far-right extremists and Republican megadonors doing everything they can to stop us. _That’s where you come in._
Sarah is ready to show up and continue her fight to improve the lives of poor and working people. [**If you stand with Sarah, please chip in to her campaign.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mcb-em-20240425?refcode=em20240425-1-167&amount=5&refcode2=167_21716_kYiHUs&akid=167%2E21716%2EkYiHUs)

* * *

* * *
My husband and I are the proud parents of six kids. So we know firsthand: **raising kids isn’t cheap.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83721008/469304808/1398971698?refcode=email_042524_Childcare&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjAyNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwOThjYjc0My0zZDAzLWVmMTEtOTZmMy03YzFlNTIxYjA3ZjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0DH4mIR0u-IUY3R-pWyghkZmm-7b7BmjokHGRA5_Qco=) And today, it’s only getting more and more expensive to raise a family here in Michigan. Why? Because we’re facing a child care crisis. In the last decade, we’ve lost 20% of our child care capacity across the country. _And in Michigan, that loss is twice as much: 40%._ Too many child care centers have been forced to close their doors, and parents are now waiting years for their children to get into the ones that have stayed open. As a result, too many young people are choosing to not even enter the workforce. **That’s why I’m leading the fight to make raising a child more affordable by passing Child Care for All in Michigan.** It is long past time that we take action to set our kids up for success, make child care affordable for parents and providers, and strengthen our workforce. Child Care for All includes a tax credit for working families, so families with young kids get money back in their pockets. It will invest in child care across the state and ease the burden so many child care providers carry. **And it will help parents achieve the Michigan Dream of earning opportunity through hard work. It’s the foundation our kids, working families, and economy need for long-term success.** At every turn in my career, I’ve worked to lower costs and open opportunities for Michigan families. I’ll never give up that fight, and if I have the honor of serving Michigan in Congress, I’ll continue to push for more funding so our kids and families can thrive. clean_body: = Kristen McDonald Rivet is leading the fight to pass Child Care for All in Michigan.= My husband and I are the proud parents of six kids. So we know firsthand: raising kids isn’t cheap. = And today, it’s only getting more and more expensive to raise a family here in Michigan. Why? Because we’re facing a child care crisis. In the last decade, we’ve lost 20% of our child care capacity across the country. And in Michigan, that loss is twice as much: 40%. Too many child care centers have been forced to close their doors, and parents are now waiting years for their children to get into the ones that have stayed open. As a result, too many young people are choosing to not even enter the workforce. That’s why I’m leading the fight to make raising a child more affordable by passing Child Care for All in Michigan. It is long past time that we take action to set our kids up for success, make child care affordable for parents and providers, and strengthen our workforce. Child Care for All includes a tax credit for working families, so families with young kids get money back in their pockets. It will invest in child care across the state and ease the burden so many child care providers carry. And it will help parents achieve the Michigan Dream of earning opportunity through hard work. It’s the foundation our kids, working families, and economy need for long-term success. At every turn in my career, I’ve worked to lower costs and open opportunities for Michigan families. I’m getting in touch because our next monthly fundraising deadline is less than a week away, and the truth is, April has been a slower-than-expected fundraising month for us. No one here is in panic mode, and the sky is certainly not falling, but we’ve got some ground to make up. [_**If you could pitch in and help us close the gap, I’d be really grateful.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83721560/469305960/-1742757043?refcode=email_042524_Long&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NTc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzNDFiM2FlMC0zZDAzLWVmMTEtOTZmMy03YzFlNTIxYjA3ZjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hnGewrvCwpfClqgdoXm15K3Wkuzz9hUrSRICLb3__gM=) But because I’m sending you this email asking for money, I also want to share a bit about what, exactly, I’m asking you to invest in, and why this campaign deserves your support. **First, the stakes of this race have become clearer, and higher, over the last few weeks.** Here in Kansas, the state Republican Party announced their support for banning same-sex marriage and taking away abortion rights, in direct opposition to the will of the voters. Then, my GOP colleagues in Congress put forward a platform to slash Social Security and Medicare, ban abortion, and criminalize IVF. Our election here in KS-03, which could determine which party controls the House of Representatives, will help decide whether or not the American people are subjected to this kind of extremism for the next two years. **Second, my background is pretty unusual for a member of Congress — let alone one representing Kansas.** I’m an LGBTQ+ Native American woman and former MMA fighter who was raised by a single mom and worked multiple jobs to pay my own way through school. That gives me a unique voice in Washington, and I’m determined to use it to deliver real progress for the people of Kansas. I’m proud to have helped create over 20,000 clean-energy jobs in our district, saved seniors money on insulin, and passed a bipartisan infrastructure law that’s kick-started construction on over 300 vital projects across the state. **And third, we are in a genuinely tough battle in this re-election campaign.** _Two_ extremist super PACs have already named me a top target, and we’re already up against misleading digital ads that attempt to smear my record in Congress. This race has been one of the most competitive and expensive in the nation the last three election cycles, but this time around, we find ourselves needing to spend money even _earlier_ to fight off the attacks we’re facing. That’s one of the reasons when we have a slow month like April, we need to pull out all the stops to try to catch up. [_**If you’ve read this far, thank you. And if, after seeing me outline what’s at stake, you’re able and willing to pitch in a few dollars, I’d be extremely grateful — because grassroots support is how we’ll overcome the attacks and win this race.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83721561/469305961/-1742757043?refcode=email_042524_Long&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NTc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzNDFiM2FlMC0zZDAzLWVmMTEtOTZmMy03YzFlNTIxYjA3ZjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hnGewrvCwpfClqgdoXm15K3Wkuzz9hUrSRICLb3__gM=) _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | | [Donate $5 →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83721562/469305962/-1742757043?refcode=email_042524_Long&amount=5&express_lane=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NTc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzNDFiM2FlMC0zZDAzLWVmMTEtOTZmMy03YzFlNTIxYjA3ZjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hnGewrvCwpfClqgdoXm15K3Wkuzz9hUrSRICLb3__gM=)

subject: Leading Gun Safety Advocates Agree: Dave Min is Right for Orange County
body:
Brady PAC Joins Sen. Min’s Coalition, Citing His Work To End Gun Violence | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/c7cc50c4d055/leading-gun-safety-advocates-agree-dave-min-is-right-for-orange-county-16195655?e=7017cc100e)
---
| |
---
| | **For Immediate Release** : April 25, 2023
**Contact** : press@davemin.com
**Leading Gun Safety Advocates Agree:
Dave Min is Right for Orange County**
_Brady PAC Joins Sen. Min’s Coalition, Citing His Work To End Gun Violence_
**IRVINE, CA** — Today, Brady PAC–leading gun violence prevention advocates–endorse Dave Min for Congress in California’s 47th Congressional District. Since before his time in the State Senate, Dave Min has centered gun violence as a top issue of his political career, campaigning in 2020 on a promise to end gun sales on the Orange County Fairgrounds. [Successful in doing so during his first year in office](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=01b418e263&e=7017cc100e), Sen. Min returned to Sacramento the next year, and [ended gun sales on all state-owned property](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=80c9493629&e=7017cc100e). He has consistently fought for greater restrictions on assault rifle ownership and ammunition sales, as well as greater accountability and safety protocols for gun owners. Min’s MAGA opponent Scott Baugh, by contrast, [solicited funds from the NRA](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=16ddb220dd&e=7017cc100e) in a fruitless attempt to avoid an embarrassing fundraising quarter.

**“Dave Min is a true champion for gun safety,”** said Ashley Lantz, executive director of Brady PAC.**“During his tenure in the State Senate, Dave has not only voted 100 percent for gun safety measures, he has authored key groundbreaking legislation around gun storage, gun dealer oversight and safety protocols, and ending gun shows on state property. He’s ready to take that fight to Washington, to ensure a safer future for our children and grandchildren.”**

Formed leading up to the 2018 midterm elections, Brady PAC was created to serve as a counterweight to “dark money” Super PACs created by the gun industry lobby. It upholds the policy ideals that have been championed by its sister organization, Brady — one of the nation’s oldest gun violence prevention grassroots advocacy organizations. Brady PAC supports candidates running for local, state, and federal office who support universal background checks, reenacting the assault weapons ban, extreme risk protection orders, and instituting other common-sense gun violence prevention legislation that will make our homes, schools, and communities safer.

The differences between Min and Baugh could not be starker. While Scott Baugh began his career as a corrupt State Assemblymember, engaging in campaign finance fraud, perjury, and obstruction of justice, which led to his being indicted for 22 criminal charges (including 4 felony counts), Dave Min began his career cracking down on corporate fraud and corruption as an SEC prosecutor. While Baugh has embraced whackjob conspiracy theories associated with white nationalism, stating that “wokeness” was a more dangerous threat to America’s security than 9/11 or World War II, Min has repeatedly celebrated diversity and stood up against hate in Orange County. And while Baugh has made clear that he would support a total abortion ban, without exceptions, even in the case of rape, incest, or danger to a woman’s life, Min has earned a 100% rating from Planned Parenthood and authored eight leading domestic violence bills into law.
###

_California’s 47th is an open Congressional District in Orange County that includes the Cities of Costa Mesa, Huntington Beach, Irvine, Newport Beach, and Seal Beach, and portions of Laguna Beach, Laguna Hills, and Laguna Woods. Incumbent Katie Porter is vacating the seat to run for U.S. Senate. In 2022, Porter defeated former Assemblymember Republican Scott Baugh by 3.44% in this “toss-up” district. State Senator Dave Min currently represents over 80% of Congressional District 47 in Sacramento. In 2020, Min received over 158,000 votes within CA-47, defeating incumbent John Moorlach by 5.15% in this area. 19% of the registered voters in CA-47 are of Asian and Pacific Islander descent, including one of the largest Korean-American populations in the country. _

Mark my words, Peter: **Gen Z will outlive the NRA.**
_The Daily Beast_ recently analyzed the NRA’s tax returns. They aren’t pretty.
In fact, the pro-gun group’s revenue has been on the decline for years now, especially since Parkland. _Last year, their fundraising was at its lowest point since 2008. And since 2018 they have lost over 1 million members._
I firmly believe that the NRA’s days are numbered—and as their power and influence fade into the dustbin of history, we will replace their corrupt, purchased politicians with a new generation of bold, courageous leaders who aren’t afraid to take urgent, necessary action to stop the scourge of gun violence in America.
**I co-founded Leaders We Deserve because Gen Z’s answer to the NRA is electing more and more young people to public office to counter their agenda.**

name: Hill Harper
subject: The Flint water crisis, 10 years later
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY HILL HARPER FOR MICHIGAN
body:
I’m on the ground in Flint to reflect on how far we’ve come.
# [](https://act.hillharper.com/go/421?t=1&akid=1193%2E62735%2ElUFrzT)
Peter,
Today marks a solemn anniversary — the **10th year since the beginning of the Flint Water Crisis.** Today, I had the opportunity to attend an event at the Flint Community Lab to reflect on how far the community has come in the wake of this environmental disaster.
To be clear, this disaster should never have happened. Once the authorities were made aware of the situation, they should have acted _immediately_ on the reports coming out of Flint, a city where more than half of all residents are Black and where a third live below the poverty line.
Ten years later, we know why that swift response never materialized: **The Michigan Civil Rights Commission concluded that the poor governmental response to the Flint crisis was a “result of systemic racism.”**
_Absolutely unacceptable._
Our leaders _must_ do better, not just for communities like Flint, but communities across the nation who bear the brunt of environmental injustice day in and day out. No more half-measures — **we need leadership that responds swiftly in crisis, puts people at the core of its work, and is committed to delivering environmental justice for all.**
I’m running for the U.S. Senate to deliver that leadership, Peter. I’m tired of watching our politicians treat people like numbers on a page, and unlike them, I’ve been showing my face in the community long before election season.
But I won’t sugarcoat anything: As a first-time candidate, I’m facing an uphill battle against better-funded and better-connected opponents on _both_ sides of the aisle. **It’s going to take all of us working together to win this race and make history in Michigan, so I hope you’ll join us in the fight for a better future.**
In solidarity,
Hill Harper
Democrat for U.S. Senate

Newest Book:
#
#### [_The Latino Century_](https://vote.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=2e84c756a73b2b9193783ffd1&id=1b6d444d4f&e=5bd167f239)
How America's Largest Minority Is Transforming Democracy
#
#### [Pre-Order Your Copy Today!](https://vote.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=2e84c756a73b2b9193783ffd1&id=57c41d1d16&e=5bd167f239)

---
|
#### An insightful investigation of how and why the two major political parties have failed to appeal to the Latino vote—the second largest ethnic voting group in the country—and the impact it will have on American democracy and politics for decades to come.
* * *
In 2020, Latinos became the second largest ethnic voting group in the country. They make up the largest plurality of residents in the most populous states in the union, as well as the fastest segment of the most important swing states in the US Electoral College. Fitting neither the stereotype of the aggrieved minority voter nor the traditional assimilating immigrant group, Latinos are challenging both political parties' notions of race, religious beliefs, economic success, and the American dream. Given their exploding numbers—and their growing ability to determine the fate of local, state, and national elections—you’d think the two major political parties would understand Latino voters. After all, their emergence on the national scene is not a new phenomenon. But they still don’t.

Republicans, not because of their best efforts but rather despite them, are just beginning to see a movement of Latinos toward the GOP. Democrats, for the moment, still win a commanding share of the Latino vote, but that share is dwindling fast. In _**The Latino Century,**_ veteran political consultant Mike Madrid uses thirty years of research and campaign experience at some of the highest levels on both sides of the aisle to address what might be the most critical questions of our time: Will the rise of Latino voters continue to foment the hyper-partisan and explosive tribalism of our age or will they usher in a new pluralism that advances the arc of social progress? How and why are both political parties so uniquely unprepared for the coming wave of Latino votes? And what must each party do to win those votes?

By answering these questions, _**The Latino Century**_ explores the true meaning of America at a time of rapid cultural change, the founding principles of self-government and individual responsibility, and one man’s journey through a political party that has turned itself inside out.

Pre-order your copy today. | | | | | | | | | Featuring Mike Madrid's Newest Book: How America's Largest Minority Is Transforming Democracy | | An insightful investigation of how and why the two major political parties have failed to appeal to the Latino vote—the second largest ethnic voting group in the country—and the impact it will have on American democracy and politics for decades to come. In 2020, Latinos became the second largest ethnic voting group in the country. They make up the largest plurality of residents in the most populous states in the union, as well as the fastest segment of the most important swing states in the US Electoral College. Fitting neither the stereotype of the aggrieved minority voter nor the traditional assimilating immigrant group, Latinos are challenging both political parties' notions of race, religious beliefs, economic success, and the American dream. Given their exploding numbers—and their growing ability to determine the fate of local, state, and national elections—you’d think the two major political parties would understand Latino voters. After all, their emergence on the national scene is not a new phenomenon. But they still don’t. Republicans, not because of their best efforts but rather despite them, are just beginning to see a movement of Latinos toward the GOP. Democrats, for the moment, still win a commanding share of the Latino vote, but that share is dwindling fast. In The Latino Century, veteran political consultant Mike Madrid uses thirty years of research and campaign experience at some of the highest levels on both sides of the aisle to address what might be the most critical questions of our time: Will the rise of Latino voters continue to foment the hyper-partisan and explosive tribalism of our age or will they usher in a new pluralism that advances the arc of social progress? How and why are both political parties so uniquely unprepared for the coming wave of Latino votes? And what must each party do to win those votes? Derek,

I was recently going through a box of old photos from the attic, and I
found one that I wanted to share with you. I think you’ll understand why.

[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=apr2024_abs_em.I2BRAI&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_GEN_GEN_AC90_20240425_PM1_V1_S1&email=&t=1004&akid=6286%2E5257348%2E4Tfwi- ]Adam being recognized by by the National Council of Senior Citizens and
the National Committee to Preserve Social Security and Medicare

That’s me being recognized by the National Council of Senior Citizens and
the National Committee to Preserve Social Security and Medicare in my
earlier days representing California in Congress.

As long as I’ve been a Democrat — from my teenage years when I listened to
scratchy vinyl recordings of RFK and JFK and Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr.,
to the present — I’ve seen the possibility and the promise of the
Democratic Party.

[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/2907?c0=apr2024_abs_em.dQ7TDg&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_GEN_GEN_AC90_20240425_PM1_V1_S1&email=&t=1005&akid=6286%2E5257348%2E4Tfwi- ]DONATE

Social Security and Medicare are two of the most successful anti-poverty
programs in American history — and Democratic presidents took on the
wealthy and corporate special interests to create both.

Franklin Roosevelt’s New Deal guaranteed a retirement income for elderly
Americans even as he pulled our economy out of the Great Depression.

Lyndon Johnson’s Medicare program ensured every senior over the age of 65
could access care, and his Great Society program made our mid-century
economy the envy of the world.

Working together with the Biden administration, I’ve fought to not only
protect these programs but to expand them — taking on Big Pharma and
Trump’s far-right megadonors to do so. We’ve taken them on, and we’ve won.

Beginning on January 1 next year, no Medicare recipient will pay more than
$35 out-of-pocket for insulin or will pay more than $2,000 all-in for that
year’s out-of-pocket prescription drug costs.

Our Inflation Reduction Act would have gone even further, allowing
Medicare to negotiate drug prices for ALL medicine, not just insulin — but
Republicans unanimously stood in our way.

Their nominee, Donald Trump, is openly suggesting cuts to Medicare and
Social Security yet again if he is elected president, just as he attempted
with every single year of his presidential budgets — and his opponents in
the primary weren’t much better.

So is my opponent, Republican Steve Garvey.

for Medicare and Social Security — a system where everyone pays their fair
share, where everyone can afford to see the doctor and fill their
prescriptions when they get sick, and where everyone can afford to retire
with dignity.

Some of this year’s most important elections aren’t getting nearly enough attention. State supreme court races play a critical role in the redistricting process. The courts have the power to review and, if necessary, overturn unfair or unconstitutional maps, not to mention rule on other critical issues. (Remember how Arizona’s bringing back an abortion ban from 1864? That’s because of a state supreme court ruling.) Having a fair-minded court is vital to upholding democratic principles and protecting our freedoms. **With so much at stake, we can’t afford NOT to get involved. We’ve identified a handful of key state supreme court races — in Michigan, Montana, North Carolina, Ohio, and Texas — as some of our TOP electoral priorities for 2024.** [**But the amount of money we’re able to invest in critical races is directly tied to the amount of money we raise from emails like this one. Please make a donation of $30 or whatever you can to help elect candidates who will champion fair maps and defend our freedoms.**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/83727874/469322550/-803236760?refcode=don_ndrc_trddnrs_email_aprfun_email_20240425-NDRC-Red-StateSupCourt_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20240425-NDRC-Red-StateSupCourt_&utm_campaign=aprfun&amount=30&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjRjYTZiZWRiLTQ4MDMtZWYxMS05NmYzLTdjMWU1MjFiMDdmOSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=BFvgWXFgLIQ1BOVjkW9svh_othv3XMUOdNvSDu7s5u0=) **By investing in state supreme court races, we can build a firewall against Republican gerrymandering.** Here are two quick examples of how state supreme courts can make or break the redistricting process: In **Wisconsin** , after over a decade of voting under egregiously gerrymandered maps, we achieved a pro-democracy majority on the state supreme court, which then issued a decision that led to the legislature enacting the fairest maps in a generation. But in **North Carolina** last year, ideologues on that state’s supreme court enabled and emboldened a highly partisan legislature to draw new maps with some of the worst gerrymandering in the country. Both states are highly competitive and evenly politically divided — but one of them has a supreme court putting its thumb on the scale to give Republicans an unfair advantage. Here’s the thing, though: **North Carolina has a supreme court seat up for grabs this fall. It’s a must-win if we want to secure fair maps and fair representation for this critical battleground state. clean_body: They can make or break the redistricting process. | Some of this year’s most important elections aren’t getting nearly enough attention. State supreme court races play a critical role in the redistricting process. The courts have the power to review and, if necessary, overturn unfair or unconstitutional maps, not to mention rule on other critical issues. (Remember how Arizona’s bringing back an abortion ban from 1864? That’s because of a state supreme court ruling.) Having a fair-minded court is vital to upholding democratic principles and protecting our freedoms. With so much at stake, we can’t afford NOT to get involved. We’ve identified a handful of key state supreme court races — in Michigan, Montana, North Carolina, Ohio, and Texas — as some of our TOP electoral priorities for 2024. = By investing in state supreme court races, we can build a firewall against Republican gerrymandering. Here are two quick examples of how state supreme courts can make or break the redistricting process: In Wisconsin , after over a decade of voting under egregiously gerrymandered maps, we achieved a pro-democracy majority on the state supreme court, which then issued a decision that led to the legislature enacting the fairest maps in a generation. But in North Carolina last year, ideologues on that state’s supreme court enabled and emboldened a highly partisan legislature to draw new maps with some of the worst gerrymandering in the country. Both states are highly competitive and evenly politically divided — but one of them has a supreme court putting its thumb on the scale to give Republicans an unfair advantage. Here’s the thing, though: North Carolina has a supreme court seat up for grabs this fall. It’s a must-win if we want to secure fair maps and fair representation for this critical battleground state. And it’s one of our top electoral priorities for 2024. = Thank you, The NDRC | = = Since 2017, the NDRC has executed a comprehensive redistricting strategy that shifts the redistricting power, creating fair districts where Democrats can compete. I am getting involved in the Ohio Senate race because there’s too much at stake.

We have two clear options:

1. **Bernie Moreno:** An America First fighter who will stand with President Trump.
2. Sherrod Brown: A liberal career politician who votes with Chuck Schumer and Joe Biden almost 100% of the time.

Now more than ever, we must rally around the BEST candidates to help us FLIP seats to win back a Senate majority – and one of those candidates is Bernie.

He’s lived the modern American dream, proving that with hard work and determination, ANYONE can build a better life for themselves in the greatest country in the world.

subject: 🚨 Special Edition: Hate Speech Crisis on Campus!
body:
ALL NEW No Doubt About It Podcast for dpwillis67@gmail.com | | | | | |
---
[](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=4355e92c53&e=567664f14c)
This is a [special edition of the No Doubt About It Podcast](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=344425bfee&e=567664f14c) addressing campus hate directed at Jewish students. The hate has even come to UNM!
[](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=3dcc93fe5b&e=567664f14c)
In this episode, we're joined by former federal prosecutor Reeve Swainston to discuss the alarming rise of open anti-Semitism on college campuses. From students and terrorist agitators openly declaring "we are Hamas" to anti-Jewish rap songs at UNM and protests shutting down schools, this hateful trend is spreading across the country, even reaching institutions like the University of New Mexico. We delve into how and why this hate is being accepted and what must be done to address it.
[Stream Episode Now](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=5757ab6ca7&e=567664f14c)
But that's not all – we also tackle the FBI's decision to no longer require cities to report crime stats, leading to misleading data that obscures the reality of increasing crime rates. Plus, we discuss Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham's special legislative session to address crime, with doubts about the effectiveness of potential crime bills.
[Stream Episode Now](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=c72165fd0f&e=567664f14c)
And on a local note, we explore the rise of carjacking in Albuquerque using AR-15s, raising concerns about how to control this dangerous trend.
Listen to the episode now and be part of the conversation!

➡ [**STREAM EPISODE NOW**](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=b6268b1342&e=567664f14c)

Workers at a Volkswagen plant in Chattanooga, Tennessee overwhelmingly voted to join the United Auto Workers union last week — despite 6 Republican governors trying to scare them into voting no. **These Republicans’ fearmongering made even clearer what we already knew: that the GOP is the party of the ultra-wealthy and powerful,_not_ the party of working people.** They’ve fought for decades, from state legislatures to Capitol Hill, to weaken our right to organize and keep power in the hands of CEOs. **[To elect representatives who will fight for workers everywhere and pass policies to support organized labor, pitch in and fuel our organizing for Working Families champions Last week’s vote made massive waves in the labor movement. The South has historically been a tough terrain for labor organizing, with the percentage of Southern workers in a union last year barely hitting 1/3 of the national average. But following massive union wins last year — including the United Auto Workers securing much-needed raises, better work conditions, and increased job security — **workers everywhere are seeing how organizing their workplace can change their lives for the better.** This win in Chattanooga marks the first auto plant in the South to vote to unionize since the 1940s. And next month, a Mercedes plant in Alabama will be holding its own union election, with most workers having already signed cards signaling their support for unionization. **Giving workers the power of a union at these plants and more in the South means that they can demand the treatment they deserve and stand up to the greedy CEOs and executives trying to fill their pockets until they burst.** That’s why Republicans are more than just furious. They’re _scared._ They know that their control relies on the megadonor class pumping absurd amounts of money into our elections, which is why they’ll throw working people and the unions created to protect them under the bus every time. From passing right-to-work laws that weaken union power across the country, to voting against the PRO Act which would expand union eligibility and protect employees from union-busting, to publicly bashing the unions and union leaders fighting for better working conditions — Republicans have a proven record of attacking organized labor. **[We’re proud to support champions who are on the side of working people and are building grassroots movements to reach voters before election day. Giving workers the power of a union at these plants and more in the South means that they can demand the treatment they deserve and stand up to the greedy CEOs and executives trying to fill their pockets until they burst. That’s why Republicans are more than just furious. They’re scared. They know that their control relies on the megadonor class pumping absurd amounts of money into our elections, which is why they’ll throw working people and the unions created to protect them under the bus every time. From passing right-to-work laws that weaken union power across the country, to voting against the PRO Act which would expand union eligibility and protect employees from union-busting, to publicly bashing the unions and union leaders fighting for better working conditions — Republicans have a proven record of attacking organized labor. Friend,

_The New York Times_ is writing a story filled with frivolous lies about my childhood.

If it weren't so demeaning to my parents' lifelong teaching careers and the town I'm so proud to have been raised in, it might be funny.

The simple fact is _The New York Times_ is lying.

**Here's the truth : and I hope you will read all the way to the end. **

Dear Peter,
Right now, we are facing monumental challenges that could shape our nation for generations to come, and the solutions we need _cannot be found_ in the status quo.
With stakes this high, stepping forward with determination is our only option. But before I go on, _I need to ask you to stay in this fight with me._

---
I can win this election, but we can't do it without your help. _And here are three reasons why we must win:_
|
1. I believe that neither President Biden nor President Trump will navigate us through the looming debt crisis that threatens our country's very foundation.
2. Their strategies fall short in confronting the perpetual foreign conflicts. There’s no sign that either will halt the relentless cycle of these forever wars.
3. Nor do I see them severing the ties of vested interests that have led to the corporate capture of crucial agencies — whether it’s the Military Industrial Complex’s hold on the CIA, Big Pharma’s influence on the NIH, CDC, and FDA, or the USDA’s sway under Big Ag.

---
---
[](https://www.kennedy24.com/donate?e=d33e868971601c1c714cfe0555abd394&utm_source=joinkennedy&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=my_mission_4_25_24_uo_nd1&n=9)
---
If either Biden or Trump are elected, change will only graze the surface; we’re likely to see minor shifts in policy areas like taxation or abortion rights, but not the sweeping reforms we so desperately need.
No, they won’t dismantle our democracy within their term—the resilience of American institutions is formidable—their presidencies are simply not set to veer away from the well-worn path of politics as usual.
But here stands a chance—an opportunity for me to pivot the nature of our governance, to rejuvenate the spirit of our democracy, and to rebuild our nation's standing on a global scale.
| | **"Here stands a chance—an opportunity for me to pivot the nature of our governance."**
---
—Robert F. Kennedy, Jr.
This is about instilling a foreign policy not predicated on the show of military might but on the strength of our economy and the power of our values.
The possibility of enacting such pivotal change, of steering our country back to its principled course, is a calling too pivotal to ignore.
That's why the thought of backing down from this contest doesn’t cross my mind.
The prospect of what we can achieve together is immense, demanding unwavering commitment and a relentless pursuit of the vision we share for America.

| | Peter, my motto has always been that when you love this country, you fight for the people who make it work. That's what I'm doing every day in the Senate.

**I'm fighting for the Dignity of Work.** No matter where you're from or what kind of work you do, hard work should pay off for everyone. Whether you punch a clock or swipe a badge, earn a salary or make tips, are raising children or caring for an aging parent, I'll fight for you.

**I'm fighting for accountability.** For years, we've seen corporations lobby for tax breaks and bad trade deals that hurt workers. I'm not afraid to stand up to Wall Street or take on Big Pharma to level the playing field.

**I'm fighting for our fundamental rights.** My opponent has made it clear he doesn’t have our best interests at heart. I will always fight for a more equal and inclusive country.

**But here's the deal, Peter:** I need you to fight with me. I'm facing my toughest race yet, and polls show me neck and neck with my Trump-backed opponent. He’s spending millions of dollars to flip this seat and the Senate red, and I can't fight back without your help.

[**_I need to raise $50,000 by midnight tonight to fight back, and I'm counting on your grassroots support to get there. subject: Sick of losing
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
It would be easy to write Kari Lake off as unserious — but it’s also a huge mistake. She is one of the most dangerous politicians in the entire country.
#

Peter, Kari Lake isn’t going to go down without a fight.
Back in 2022, she lost her campaign for governor by less than 20,000 votes.
Since then, she’s put up more lawsuits than we can count trying to dispute the results of that election. Most recently, she took her election denial all the way to the Supreme Court. They dismissed her case earlier this week.
After all those defeats it would be easy to write Kari Lake off as unserious — but it’s also a huge mistake. She is one of the most dangerous politicians in the entire country.
That 2022 campaign she lost? It was by less than one percent of all votes cast, and it was anyone’s guess who would come out on top until the very last minute.
She’s almost certainly learned a thing or two since then, and we’re seeing that play out now. She’s raising a ton of cash, she’s racking up endorsements from the MAGA-right to the GOP establishment, and the polls show this race is neck-and-neck.
We have no room for error. If we want to defeat Kari Lake one more time we are going to have to work like hell to get the job done.
And to be perfectly honest with you, we don’t have a shot at victory without your support.

It's why, as a United States Senator, I fought to keep judges off the bench who didn't support reproductive freedom. Peter, before I ask you to chip in to help us win in Ohio and keep the Senate blue, I want to take a moment to explain what our fight is all about.

**I've said it before, and I'll say it again: When you love this country, you fight for the people who make it work.** Whether you punch a clock or swipe a badge, earn a salary or work for tips, are raising children or caring for an elderly parent, I will _always_ fight for you.

Whether it's capping the cost of insulin, demanding better wages, or working to enshrine reproductive freedoms into law, I'm fighting for the issues that matter most to Ohioans. Because that is what I was elected to do.

**My self-funding opponent, Bernie Moreno, on the other hand, has proven time and time again that he _does not care_ what the people of Ohio want.** Instead, he's focused on cozying up to Donald Trump and advancing the MAGA agenda – from passing a national abortion ban to cutting taxes for his megadonor friends.

The people of Ohio, and our country, deserve better than that. But the odds are stacked against me: **Polls show me and Moreno neck and neck – in the race that experts say will decide Senate control. That's why we set a goal to raise $50,000 before our midnight deadline, and I'm counting on you to help me reach it.**

# Twisting Laws to Fit an Agenda
---
| |
---
|
---
|
The Biden administration is now using the Emergency Medical Treatment and Active Labor Act ([EMTALA](https://saveamernow.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=bfee6d8faa8bd945842640631&id=48c6a88b5d&e=c50c08d277)) to override pro-life laws in 20 states. At its core, this outrageous move forces hospitals to perform abortions in the name of “emergency care” — in stark opposition to the _actual intent_ of the legislation. Now, instead of ensuring emergency care for the most vulnerable, this law is being used to force pro-abortion ideology into emergency rooms and place the unborn at risk.

EMTALA was meant to protect mothers and their unborn children by ensuring emergency care for the indigent and uninsured. Instead, Biden’s DOJ wants to use it as a weapon against pro-life laws, mandating abortions in emergency rooms — an action that is unfortunately in keeping with the rest of his radical leftist agenda.

This blatant misuse of EMTALA goes against both its original intent and pro-life principles. We need to take action and fight back against this encroachment on our values.

Again, this serves to highlight the importance of the work we do together. We must take action to shift the balance of power in Washington and elect candidates with the moral backbone to do the right thing. Our nation is at a crossroads, and the leftist agenda threatens to erode our freedoms further each day. It’s time to take a stand, together, and **Save America Now**.

We have to catch up. Fast. But I’m about to say something that would make my finance director’s head spin—**the amount you give doesn’t matter to me. Here’s why:**

I’m proud to run this campaign _the right way_ —with over 500,000 individual contributions from folks like you powering everything we do.

Peter,

Students across the country are bravely standing up to genocide and
demanding their universities divest from arms dealers enabling the
violence in Gaza. As a result, the GOP and AIPAC-backed members of the
Democratic Party are pushing university administrations to suspend and
arrest their students for exercising their right to free speech. It’s an
appalling example of history repeating itself.

This week, Justice Democrats incumbent and Squad member Rep. Ilhan Omar —
whose daughter was suspended for participating in a peaceful
pro-Palestinian protest at Columbia University the day after Ilhan
questioned the University’s president — spoke to student protestors at the
University of Minnesota, and was promptly attacked for it.

Republican House Majority Whip Tom Emmer posted these disgustingly
Islamophobic comments about Ilhan yesterday:

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jdem-pts-email-io.6PEDYD&refcode=em20240425-34493&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1001&akid=34493%2E1203867%2ExFchXF ]Screenshot of tweet by Tom Emmer: “Propping up the violent protests
happening around our nation’s college campuses is unacceptable. Once
again, Ilhan Omar’s pro-Hamas rhetoric solidifies the Democrat party as
the pro-terrorist party. Now more than ever, we must protect Jewish
Students.” Retweet from Daily Caller: “Ilhan Omar spoke at a University of
Minnesota pro-Palestine student protest and blasted Biden and the media
for their critical response to protests nationwide.”

Protesting genocide and the suffering of innocent people in Gaza is not
anti-semitic or pro-Hamas, but Republicans like Emmer and AIPAC-funded
establishment Democrats want us to think otherwise as they continue to use
our tax dollars to send billions of unconditional aid to Netanyahu’s
military.

Ilhan is keeping up the fight for human rights both here and abroad, but
she faces a serious threat to her House seat in this August’s primary
election as AIPAC’s super PAC threatens to spend $100 million to unseat
the Squad.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jdem-pts-email-io.6PEDYD&refcode=em20240425-34493&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=34493%2E1203867%2ExFchXF ]Will you show Ilhan you have her back in this critical moment and help

Ilhan has faced Islamophobic, racist attacks like this before — but it
won’t stop her from standing on the right side of history and fighting for
our shared progressive values.

Let’s show her that she has the support of the people and ensure she has

In solidarity,

Geoff Simpson

**I’m not the only one who’s worried about**[**#RankedChoiceVoting**](https://f69e.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=662adf7e7b9a3b03ebe707b2&u=https%3A%2F%2Ftwitter.com%2Fhashtag%2FRankedChoiceVoting%3Fsrc%3Dhashtag_click&w=636d98a80d1d302f275cb244&c=b_662adf1b6a45a00dac300f8e&l=en-US&s=BAOWLZtB7Pu5v-BOjw0oVqUiRf0%3D)**impact on vulnerable voters** Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs (Democrat) to discuss his opposition to RCV. Here is what Secretary Hobbs told us: “Ranked-choice voting adds a layer of complexity to voting that threatens to disenfranchise people who aren’t experts at the process. This includes people living with developmental disabilities – such as my son – for whom choosing one candidate is more straightforward than figuring out how to rank a list of them. Additionally, it can be a challenge for newly-naturalized citizens to adapt to American elections. Converting some elections to ranked-choice voting would increase the obstacles to exercising their rights as Americans. Top-two primaries present none of these challenges. You pick your favorite, then you send in your ballot. That’s something people can easily grasp. I stand firmly behind Top Two and encourage other states to learn from our usage of it.” Secretary Hobbs also recently told Crosscut: “Oh, I have lots of feelings about ranked-choice voting. I’m completely against ranked-choice voting; I used to be for it. But when you occupy this office, you have to take a step back and look at how elections affect everyone. Right? You know, the top three things, transparency, accessibility and security is what I look at. And then just with my own personal situation, my mom came to this country, she didn’t know any English. You know, we both learned by watching Sesame Street. And then my middle son is a child with special needs. So imagine, if you will, a naturalized citizen where English is not their first language, receiving a ballot, where they have to vote by ranked choice? How are they going to do that? They don’t know how to do that . . . And that’s why I am no longer for ranked-choice voting because you will disenfranchise people. They will not take full advantage of their vote because they don’t understand what they’re doing.”

**Overview of Election Types and Systems** The recent elections comprised various types, including Special Primary, Special General, Regular Primary, and Regular General elections. Each election type presented its own set of rules and systems. Notably, both the Special General Election and the Regular Primary occurred simultaneously. The Special General employed a Top 4 Ranked Choice Voting (RCV) system, whereas the Regular Primary followed a simpler system where voters were to select just one candidate. Complexity of Simultaneous Elections The concurrent scheduling of the Special General Election (using a Top 4 RCV system) and the Regular Primary (select one candidate system) undoubtedly introduced complexities. Voters received a single ballot that included both election types, potentially leading to significant confusion. This complexity was especially pronounced because the instructions for the Regular Primary (to choose one candidate) could easily be mistaken as applicable to the Special General Election as well. Voter Confusion and Election Outcomes The confusion among voters is highlighted by the election outcomes. In the Special General, a Democrat secured victory with 75,000 votes, despite Republican candidates collectively garnering 112,000 votes. This result suggests a significant portion of voters may have followed the Regular Primary’s instructions, opting to vote for only one candidate in the Special General as well. Such a scenario would inadvertently skew the effectiveness of the RCV system, where ranking multiple candidates is crucial. Introduction of Ranked Choice Voting Adding to the electoral confusion was the introduction of Ranked Choice Voting (RCV) for Alaskans. As their first experience with RCV, many voters were unfamiliar with its mechanisms, which require voters to rank candidates by preference. The presence of both a new voting system and dual election types on the same ballot likely contributed to unintended voting behaviors and unexpected election results. Implications and Reflections The overlap of different voting instructions and the debut of RCV evidently had a profound impact on voter behavior and the election’s outcome. This scenario underscores the need for clear communication and voter education, particularly when implementing new voting technologies or systems. Ensuring that voters are well-informed and understand the distinctions between concurrent elections is crucial for the integrity and accuracy of electoral processes.

subject: Friday 7 pm Symposium: Remember the Spirit of the Elbe
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Sare for Senate

| | [](https://www.sareforsenate.com/?e=bd1d687cdeff164927fc1e159dca3e71&utm_source=sareforsenate&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=20240426_symposium&n=1)
---
Friend -- On April 25, 1945, American and Russian soldiers joyfully embraced as brothers when they finally met on the banks of the Elbe River, having finally broken the Nazi line. They knew that victory would soon follow. The Soviet Union had lost 27 million people in World War II, close to one out of every 6 Russians. No family was untouched. Sen. Chuck Schumer and his junior partner Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand can't even fathom how it looks to a Russian family for German tanks to once more be rolling toward their border, with the U.S. President expressing an intent to "weaken Russia." The House and Senate have just shamelessy voted to send nearly $100 bn more to Ukraine, Israel, and Taiwan, completely oblivious to the massive death and suffering these weapons are inflicting. I have invited historian William Jones of EIR to join me in discussing the Meeting on the Elbe, which occurred 79 years ago, in hopes that it may inspire us to revive the "better Angels" of our own national identity.

Team — We hope you’ll give us a minute to explain why your contribution to our team is fundamental to our fight to flip the House majority in our favor. Political scientists at the Cook Political Report rate districts across the country and score them based on their partisan leaning, called a partisan index. Some districts are “blue” districts and others are solidly “red,” meaning that in cycle after cycle voters are more or less guaranteed to turn out in favor of the Republican or Democrat. This gives respective parties a number of districts they can rely on to go their way each year. Fighting for the Ocean State in the Senate is an honor, and I work hard to deliver results for Rhode Islanders and Americans every single day. **That’s why today I’m excited to share with you that I’m officially running for re-election in Rhode Island for the United States Senate.** **[Will you split a $10 donation between my campaign and Tina Smith’s to help me win and defend our Democratic Senate majority?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83736495/469340655/-1605506409?amount=10&refcode=AU_TSM_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20240425_PM1_V1_S3&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTU1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmY2Q5NjdjNy01YjAzLWVmMTEtOTZmMy03YzFlNTIxYjA3ZjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=sU750LacmoMKIHG1sIqgeRIwkmtvEx68GzPas2MizCQ=)** I’ve worked tirelessly to make health care affordable and accessible, lower the cost of prescription drugs, take on corporate greed, bring the climate fight right to the big oil companies, shine a light on corruption at the Supreme Court, protect access to abortion, and stand up for American democracy. That’s a lot, but I’m proud of it; as Nancy Pelosi said: “Persistent. Relentless.” But this year, democracy itself is on the ballot. And as the chief antagonist of the dark money groups trying to bend democracy to their will, I need your help to win this thing. If you send me back to the Senate this year, I won’t stop fighting to make our government and economy work for all Americans. I’ll tackle climate change before it’s too late. I’ll defend democracy and freedom here at home and abroad. I’ll fight to put a real check on corporate power. And I’ll make sure the highest earners finally start paying their fair share. **[So I’m personally asking, will you split $10 between me and Tina Smith to help me reach my re-election launch fundraising goal, win in Rhode Island, and keep the Senate blue?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83736496/469340656/-1605506409?amount=10&refcode=AU_TSM_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20240425_PM1_V1_S3&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTU1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmY2Q5NjdjNy01YjAzLWVmMTEtOTZmMy03YzFlNTIxYjA3ZjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=sU750LacmoMKIHG1sIqgeRIwkmtvEx68GzPas2MizCQ=)** Thank you for all of your support. I’ll defend democracy and freedom here at home and abroad. I’ll fight to put a real check on corporate power. And I’ll make sure the highest earners finally start paying their fair share. = Thank you for all of your support. body:

It’s official: [**a second Republican challenger has announced a campaign to run against me for Senate.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/2117?t=8&akid=2142%2E4032634%2Effs9pq) The thing is, this candidate only officially registered as a Republican on February 29 this year. He was previously unregistered, and before that he was a registered Democrat.

So I’m running for Senate against a self-funder from Rhode Island, and a 56-day-old Republican. I want to be clear: I am still taking this race very seriously. Because we can’t underestimate the amount of support my opponents can receive from national Republicans and outside special interests. We can’t underestimate the threat of Republicans controlling the Senate, passing a national abortion ban, and other extremist items that have been on Donald Trump’s agenda. And we can’t underestimate what would happen if our progressive movement for big, structural change loses its momentum. **The amount that we raise right now in response to my opponents’ announcements will determine how strong we can compete — and how much we can invest in campaigning for our plans and growing popularity for them.** [**Unlike my opponents, this campaign is funded solely by grassroots donors. So if you’re able, I need you to pitch in $25 or anything you can right now to help guarantee I can compete and keep fighting for working families in the Senate.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/2117?amount=25&t=9&akid=2142%2E4032634%2Effs9pq)

Hello,
After the 2022 election, my husband Adam Frisch and I went to Washington for “freshman orientation” for new members of Congress.
We still didn’t know whether or not Adam had defeated Lauren Boebert. We were in the middle of a recount – and Adam was down by only a few hundred votes.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83736772/469341520/1610638071?refcode=em20240425pm-nd&amounts=5%2C10%2C25%2C35%2C50%2C100%2C250&refcode2=e6a4b958-5d03-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&recurring=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjIxNiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlNmE0Yjk1OC01ZDAzLWVmMTEtOTZmMy03YzFlNTIxYjA3ZjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=5dHsfB78-cdsCA7h9kHIpjKUMLsdDVg9qj9j6P5mOBo=)
Ultimately, though, after all the votes were counted, Adam came up short. We lost to Boebert by just 546 votes. It was the closest race in the entire country.
Now, Adam’s running again in 2024 – and with Lauren Boebert now out of the race, I know he can win this time. But first, we have to fix the reason he so narrowly lost in 2022.
**During the last campaign, we got out-spent – by millions and millions of dollars.** It wasn’t that we didn’t put in the work (we did). It wasn’t that Adam didn’t have a positive vision for the district (he does). We were just drowned out in millions of dollars of lie-filled attack ads.
**If Adam’s going to be able to finish the job and win this critical seat, we cannot afford to get out-spent again – and we’re counting on your help now.**
**We’ve set a goal to raise another $35,000 before our fundraising deadline at midnight tonight, but right now, we still have $4,608 left to raise.**
[**Please, can my husband Adam Frisch count on you to chip in $5 or more right now to his campaign – every dollar you can afford before our fundraising deadline – and help him win this critical seat and replace Lauren Boebert in Congress?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83736773/469341521/1610638071?refcode=em20240425pm-nd&amounts=5%2C10%2C25%2C35%2C50%2C100%2C250&refcode2=e6a4b958-5d03-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&recurring=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjIxNiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlNmE0Yjk1OC01ZDAzLWVmMTEtOTZmMy03YzFlNTIxYjA3ZjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=5dHsfB78-cdsCA7h9kHIpjKUMLsdDVg9qj9j6P5mOBo=)

We were on our way to an unprecedented 3-way general election this November _**until a former staffer and donor of our opponent called for a recount.**_

Now, our campaign didn’t call for this recount. Recounts are expensive and grueling — but we’re confident that when all the votes are counted, we’ll be on our way to the general election in November.
